To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the higher education financing policies of the Pinochet, Aylwin and Frei administrations have had a positive impact in the expansion of access to higher education for all socio-economic groups; (b) these policies have had a negative impact in the access to higher education of the lower, lower-middle and middle-income students; and (c) these policies have increased the access to higher institutions of upper and upper-middle class students.

“The Chilean higher education system has been more successful in increasing the number of students attending higher education than in providing equal access to higher education for all socio-economic groups.”
the Chilean higher education system is characterized by a high level of stratification, and the system is not accessible to lower socio-economic groups.

the impact of the financing policies implemented in Chile during the 1990s, in particular with the effect that the new policies had on the access of different income groups to post-secondary education.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the higher education policies implemented during the Pinochett and the Frei administrations have been more successful in increasing the enrollment rate and in improving the access of upper-middle income families than in improving the access to higher education of lower, lower-middle and middle income families.
, during the Pinocher, the Aylwin and the Frei administrations, the access to post-secondary institutions has increased, but it is still unequal and it is more unequal in the private sector.
, during the 1980–1998 period, higher education financing policies were not able to reduce the inequalities in access to higher levels of education in Chile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the higher education system has been transformed from one of mass higher education for the middle and upper classes to a more stratified system of access and opportunity.
the higher education financing system in Chile has produced a higher education system with a greater proportion of students from higher socio-economic groups.

, while the Chilean government has been able to expand higher education participation, it has done so in a way that has created inequalities in access and that the current system has not been able to provide a more equal access to higher education for the lower and lower middle income groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Chilean case is a useful example of how the combination of market forces and public policies in higher education can produce unequal access and unequal opportunities in the context of a market-based system.

the higher education financing policies that Chile implemented during the 1990s did not succeed in creating equalities in access, but rather created (in) equal opportunities for different social groups.

the impact of structural adjustment and subsequent post-adjustment higher education policies on access to higher education was highly differentiated by income level and that the policies were not successful in reducing the gap between the access to higher education of the different socio-economic groups, particularly between the lower and the upper-middle income levels.
